## Trial `encrypted-volume-ubuntu24__aCft9xu`

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **encrypted-volume-created — Satisfied:** Provide an encrypted (LUKS) volume on node1
  - **Why:** cryptsetup luksFormat --type luks2 succeeded on a file-backed image, followed by a successful luksOpen creating /dev/mapper/secure_srv.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0c233bfd7c16448f`, `cmd-4ecb8872b3c2460e`
- **mounted-at-srv-secure — Satisfied:** Volume is mounted at /srv/secure
  - **Why:** ext4 filesystem created on the mapper device and mounted at /srv/secure; a test file was written and read back, and post-reboot df/lsblk confirm the mount from /dev/mapper/secure_srv.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-07351a574931421f`, `cmd-d325bacba98c4f6b`
- **auto-unlock-mount-at-boot — Satisfied:** Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot with no manual intervention
  - **Why:** crypttab/fstab entries were added, systemd generated systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service and srv-secure.mount pulled into local-fs.target. A genuine node reboot was triggered (systemctl reboot), boot_id changed from f9bf293d... to e7733aa3..., and post-restart evidence shows systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service succeeded automatically, srv-secure.mount is active, and the pre-existing test file content ('hello') was intact — demonstrating the full boot-time unlock/mount transition without manual action.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3e4994f88dfd4599`, `cmd-366b379c6a334808`, `cmd-d5b0405031514283`, `cmd-1fbb0d6de7c545fd`, `cmd-46adb7d431ef4bb6`, `cmd-d325bacba98c4f6b`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **1.000**. All state-changing commands map directly to the task: keyfile creation, image creation, LUKS format/open, filesystem creation and mount, crypttab/fstab edits, and the umount+luksClose/systemctl start cycle used only to verify the generator-created units work before trusting a real reboot. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were found; failed-services lists are empty both before and after, and listening-socket/temp-file diffs are attributable solely to the reboot itself (new ephemeral PIDs/private-tmp dirs), not to executor actions. ### Comments and limitations

- The keyfile enabling automatic unlock is stored unencrypted on the root filesystem (root-only permissions); this is an inherent trade-off for boot-time auto-unlock without a TPM/network-bound mechanism and was not flagged as an issue by the task, but represents a lower security bar than passphrase-only LUKS.
- Evidence for the reboot is a single successful cycle; no additional failure-mode testing (e.g., missing keyfile, corrupted image) was performed, though none was required by the task.
- Verifier confidence was 0.950; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
